milestone: M12 External Mode Pack Execution Policy

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Direct external active Mode Pack tasks are bound to runtime-owned active snapshot identity at task.run.
Rust denies stale active policy before execution side effects.
Headless callers can resume external active Mode Pack tasks without caller-side policy reconstruction.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances mode_pack_runtime with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: Direct external active Mode Pack task.run requires the current active snapshot and compiled policy to match task-start provenance.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing live-file provenance does not bind active replacement or rollback snapshots at the point of use.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Delayed tasks admitted under an old active Mode Pack can execute after active policy changes.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from recent M56 Golden Journey phases and older M12/M21 Mode Pack handoff, child, activation, and live-file revalidation work.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Uses existing task.start and task.run.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. Adds no report, history, digest, readiness, verdict, preview, dashboard, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: task.run denies stale active snapshot source, activation fingerprint, mode, or policy fingerprint before TaskRunning.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless controllers receive deterministic execution or denial without inspecting raw Mode Pack state.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the direct active-snapshot execution-policy gap for external Mode Packs.
